biography.plain_text: Hubert Palfinger was an Austrian industrialist who transformed his father Richard's workshop into an international crane manufacturer. Born in Grieskirchen and trained as a machine fitter, he developed the Salzburg-based family business and took it public. His sons Hubert junior and Hannes later represented the family on its supervisory board.

long_biography.plain_text:
Under Hubert Palfinger's leadership, the crane manufacturer bearing his name developed equipment that could reach further without taking up more space on a lorry. A patented folding main boom allowed long cranes to be packed away compactly. Serial production and early exports to Switzerland and France helped move the business beyond its original market.

Cleaning and repainting commercial ships became another engineering problem for Palfinger. He funded a separate venture, Hubert Palfinger Technologies, to automate the work. Its equipment used high-pressure water to remove old coatings, captured the residue and applied fresh paint more evenly. The process reduced airborne paint waste and won an Energy Globe award in the air category. Palfinger formed a joint venture with the Chinese repair company IMC-YY to bring the technology to more shipyards.

Family succession and eventual economic ownership support Marriage / family transfer. No precise transfer deed or inheritance mechanism was established. Calling him the group's founder in some tributes does not erase his father's pre-existing workshop or justify self-made independent status.

Manufacturing at death is a reasoned inference from retained core ownership and the related machinery venture, not a claim to a complete private balance sheet. The origin-sector fallback was considered but positive near-terminal ownership supports a current terminal sector assessment.

The terminal relationship is evaluated against the principal original crane fortune. Explicit operational withdrawal and continuing family participation support Heir / family shareholder. He remained an active HPT founder; the separate venture had consumed large development funding but had not demonstrated comparable wealth generation, so its role does not automatically replace the core relationship.

The estate's bankruptcy is directly confirmed by the company's 2021 financial statements. This limits any terminal valuation claim, but does not establish that all family-foundation interests were estate property or extinguish the independently reported lifetime stake. Debts, company receivables and family guarantees are kept separate.

Exact death date is fully verified, but the immutable Alive inventory excludes the death fields from researchable missing details. They remain candidate facts pending mortality correction; the inventory and input are not altered. Middle names and secondary nationality remain unverified.
